explanation: Kingdom Fungi contains over 80,000 species. While some species are unicellular, most fungi are multicellular. Fungi are heterotrophic organisms that consume organic matter, acting primarily as saprotrophs that absorb nutrients from dead or decaying matter in their environment. Kingdom Fungi is divided into 5 Phyla. Because fungi do not fossilize well, it is difficult to examine their fossil record.

questions.q: How do saprotrophic fungi acquire nutrients?
opts: By engulfing other microorganisms via phagocytosis
By absorbing organic matter, usually dead or decaying, from their surroundings
By using solar energy to synthesize sugars
By oxidizing hydrogen gas and carbon dioxide
questions.exp: The notes state that saprotrophs 'absorb this organic matter' which is 'Usually dead or decaying matter from surroundings'.

questions.q: Why is it difficult to examine the evolutionary record of Kingdom Fungi?
opts: Fungi did not exist before the 20th century.
Fungi only live inside other living hosts.
questions.exp: The notes explicitly mention that fungi 'Do not fossilize well, hard to examine fossil record'.
